newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Welteke says dollar correction was needed.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Welteke says dollar correction was needed.

text.p: German Bundesbank council member Ernst Welteke said on Monday that the recent correction of the mark from its overvalued state was necessary.

"The dollar correction was necessary but the appreciation cannot continue at the pace we have seen since January," Welteke said. He added that "such a change was ultimately necessary to rule out the danger of inflation."

"The situation in foreign exchange markets, where the mark was overvalued after 1995's Mexico crisis, also fit in well with a more positive overall picture," Welteke told journalists at a dinner in Frankfurt.
The recent revaluation contributed to a more positive picture of the German economy.
The dollar stood at around 1.70 marks on Monday night, slightly below earlier highs, but still stronger than for many months.

Compared to the situation at the end of 1995, when the German currency's was at its most overvalued, the mark had fallen six percent compared to the 18 industrial nations and 16 percent against the dollar, Welteke said.

Welteke, who is also president of the central bank of the state of Hesse, was speaking at a dinner organised by the International Business Journalists Forum. (( --Clifford Coonan, Frankfurt Newsroom +49 69 756525))
